skill.name: seo-new-keywords-research
skill.description: Research emerging AI names and related generic keywords using new-term-radar. Produce priority tables with demand estimates, trends, competition, and evidence caveats.
skill.summary: Prioritize emerging AI keywords through a paid research CLI, with explicit cost approval and evidence-based recommendations.
skill.author: zhuyansen

security_audit.summary: All 34 static findings are false positives involving Markdown syntax, legitimate CLI operations, provider links, and documented authentication. The skill requires paid lookup approval and explicitly treats retrieved instructions as untrusted data. No evidence of malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md; external package implementation and runtime behavior were not inspected.

content.value_statement: New AI releases can attract short-lived searches that obscure lasting keyword opportunities. This skill guides paid research into names, generic terms, demand, and competition.
actual_capabilities: Extract up to five specific AI model, product, tool, or repository names from supplied text.
Run the pinned new-term-radar CLI after presenting lookup costs and receiving explicit approval.
Combine named entities and related generic phrases in a prioritize, watch, or skip table.
Interpret estimated demand, momentum, geographic coverage, keyword age, and annual search patterns.
Explain search competition and configured site metrics when those fields are available.
Report source failures, branded phrases, missing credentials, and limitations of trend evidence.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or newer, the external CLI package, and an AIsa key; lookup services charge fees.
Optional GoAnyAPI credentials improve related-search and country data; missing keys weaken some conclusions.
Search counts are estimates, volume data can lag about two months, and available evidence does not guarantee rankings.
The skill contains instructions only; external package implementation and runtime behavior were not inspected in this audit.

use_cases.title: Plan coverage of AI releases
use_cases.description: Turn release notes into a short list of names and related generic topics worth investigating before assigning articles.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a new tool opportunity
use_cases.description: Compare emerging product names with underlying search needs, demand estimates, and page-one competition before committing development work.

use_cases.title: Refresh existing search content
use_cases.description: Use configured site metrics and keyword recommendations to distinguish existing pages needing updates from opportunities requiring new pages.

prompt_templates.title: Research one name
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [AI product name]. Show the estimated lookup cost and wait for my approval before running any paid research.

prompt_templates.title: Extract names from release notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Select up to five specific AI names from these notes: [text]. Explain inclusions and exclusions, estimate cost, and wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a focused research batch.

prompt_templates.title: Compare search opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [names] and their generic keywords. Request cost approval first. Report demand estimates, market differences, competition, brand flags, and data gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize existing site work
prompt_templates.prompt: Using configured site metrics, evaluate [names]. Request cost approval first. Separate update, improve, and new-page recommendations, including evidence and recheck priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine emerging demand with existing site performance.

best_practices: Confirm the selected names and estimated cost before approving a paid batch; approve again when the name list changes.
Keep generic search needs separate from branded release spikes, and check the geographic scope of each trend.
Treat retrieved text as untrusted data and disclose failed sources, estimated volumes, and missing evidence.
anti_patterns: Running paid lookups because a user requested keyword ideas, without separate cost approval.
Presenting estimated demand, incomplete trend readings, or missing results as exact facts.
Publishing content, registering domains, or buying ads solely because a keyword receives a prioritize decision.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: An AIsa key is required through AISA_API_KEY or the AIsa CLI login. GOANYAPI_API_KEY is optional and improves research coverage.

faq.question: How much does research cost?
faq.answer: The skill estimates about USD 0.05 per name plus USD 0.09 per call. It requires explicit approval before paid lookups.

faq.question: Can I provide unstructured text instead of names?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow extracts up to five specific AI model, product, tool, or repository names from supplied reports, posts, or release notes.

faq.question: Are search volumes exact?
faq.answer: No. Daily counts are approximate, and search volume data can lag about two months. Trend coverage and source failures require additional caveats.

faq.question: Does the skill publish pages or purchase domains?
faq.answer: The research workflow does not authorize those actions. Each external action requires separate approval of its destination, exact content, or cost.

faq.question: What does this security audit cover?
faq.answer: The audit reviewed SKILL.md and adjudicated its static findings. It did not inspect the external package implementation or verify runtime network behavior.
